title: 1955 AHSME Problem 37
statement: A three-digit number has, from left to right, the digits \(h,\) \(t,\) and \(u\) with \(h>u.\) When the number with the digits reversed is subtracted from the original number, the units’ digit in the difference is \(4.\) The next two digits, from right to left, are:

solutions.text:
The difference is \(99(h-u).\) Since \(h-u\) is an integer from \(1\) through \(9,\) and the units digit is \(4,\) we need \(9(h-u)\equiv4\pmod{10}.\) This gives \(h-u=6,\) so the difference is \[ 99\cdot6=594. \] Moving from right to left after the units digit \(4,\) the next digits are \(9\) and \(5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Find the digit \(h-u\) for which \(99(h-u)\) ends in \(4\)
